added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer - Security Clearance Required
added.description:
About Virtru:

While the rest of the security industry obsesses over locking data down to prevent it from being lost or stolen, we're doing something fundamentally different at Virtru. We're setting data free so that you can intentionally share it with others, but without sacrificing security, privacy, or control.

We've created both a suite of powerful data protection applications and an open platform that's sparking an ecosystem of innovation. Through the Trusted Data Format (TDF) open standard, we're not just protecting data; we're creating a new paradigm where security enables sharing rather than preventing it.

Think of us as the Android of data protection: a robust platform with an open core that developers and partners can build upon, coupled with our own best-in-class applications that showcase what's possible when you reimagine security from the ground up.

Backed by Iconiq Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Foundry Capital, and Tiger Global, we're helping Fortune 500 companies and government agencies discover that true data security means having the freedom to share, collaborate, and innovate — without compromise.

Compensation: $200,000-225,000/year

Team & Position Details:

Virtru protects data wherever it travels, for customers ranging from commercial enterprises to the Department of Defense, the Intelligence Community, Law Enforcement, and Federal Civilian agencies. Many of these customers run Virtru inside classified mission environments across the Washington, DC region, where the work happens on site next to the customer's own engineers, and where what we ship has to fit systems few people outside the building can see.

As a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer in the Delivery Engineering organization, you'd be helping to build a founder team focused on making these deployments simple, easy, and fast. You'll be the senior engineer who can change the software in the room. You'll design and build the integrations, policy enforcement points (the components that enforce access policy inside a customer's application), and deployment tooling our customers need and cannot get from the product alone, and you'll own the technical outcome of each deployment from zero to one and on into production. You'll be embedded with one cleared mission customer and own that account's technical outcome end to end. This location requires a full-scope polygraph

You will work with deployment engineers who run installs and upgrades through our published paths, with solutions architects who shaped each engagement, with QA to prove what you build before it ships, and with our product engineering and Platform Engineering counterparts, who need what you learn in the field as designs and decisions they can act on. You'll also help set the bar for the forward deployed engineers who join after you.

The impact of this role is company and product wide, heavily enabling our goals to scale Virtru, partner, and customer led deployments non-linearly without having to throw more humans at the problem. You'll be expected to come up with AI-native design patterns that will increase our velocity without compromising our high bar for quality and security. The right candidate is excited about working on a small, nimble, highly autonomous and empowered team where everyone is expected to make high judgement, high velocity decisions independently and with urgency. If you want a role where the connection between what you build and what the customer achieves requires no explaining, this is one.

As a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, your responsibilities will include:

Design and ship software inside cleared customer environments.
Integrations, policy enforcement points, connectors, and deployment tooling, written in Go, Python, Java, or Rust, reviewed, tested with QA, and built so the next customer can reuse them.
Own the technical outcome of each deployment you're staffed to.
From the first environment review through production and upgrade, you are the engineer accountable for the platform working in the customer's systems, across Kubernetes, Windows estates, identity providers, and air-gapped classified networks.
Turn field lessons into product decisions.
Write designs and architecture decision records that weigh a product fix against a field workaround, take them to our product engineering teams with evidence, and see them through to a decision.
Resolve conflicts between a customer's accreditation boundary and the platform's requirements by changing the design, and write the pattern down so the next engagement inherits it.
Diagnose failures down to source code, whether the cause sits in our software, in the customer's environment, or in the space between them.
Build validated configurations for identity providers beyond our reference setup, such as PingFederate, Entra ID, and Okta, so the next customer configures what you built instead of starting over.
Work inside codebases other teams own, and leave them better tested and documented than you found them.
Package what you build so it installs, upgrades, and runs in disconnected environments under STIG hardening and FIPS constraints.
Partner with deployment engineers so standard installs follow the published path, and hand them what you build with documentation, test evidence, and a clear way to report back.
Explain your designs to customer security reviewers and accrediting officials, and answer their follow-up questions.
Mentor other forward deployed engineers, review their code and designs, and help define how we interview and level for the role.
Use AI coding agents as part of your daily workflow, and help the team learn which patterns raise quality and speed together.
This role requires residence in the DMV and on-site work at customer locations at least 50% of the time, and may require travel to other customer sites in the DC region.

Skills that will help you thrive in this role:

Must haves

An active TS/SCI US security clearance.
The Fort Meade location also requires a full-scope polygraph. This role will work in classified environments at least 50% of the time.
You ship production code today, and other people reuse what you design.
You write and review code in Go, Python, Java, or Rust as part of your current job, and you can walk us through a component you designed that another team or customer adopted.
You have made software work in environments you did not build.
You have diagnosed identity, certificate, or Kubernetes failures in a classified, accredited, or customer production environment from logs, without the original author on the call, and changed a design to fit the environment rather than asking for an exception.

Nice to haves

Kubernetes across more than one distribution, such as OpenShift, Rancher, or RKE2, including Helm packaging.
Delivering software into air-gapped environments: offline registries, bundle transfer, and upgrades with no network.
Identity and authorization integration: OIDC, SAML, PingFederate, Entra ID, Okta, CAC or PIV, and attribute-based access control (ABAC).
Windows and .NET depth: Windows Services, signed installers, Active Directory, and Group Policy.
DISA STIGs, FIPS 140, and the Risk Management Framework from the delivery side.
Familiarity with Zero Trust security architecture and concepts such as Policy Enforcement and Decision Points, cryptography, and identity.
Design documents or decision records another team adopted.
Experience building with AI coding agents.
Prior forward deployed, embedded, or customer-site engineering work with Intelligence Community or Department of Defense customers.

Where this role may not be a fit

Having stepped away from writing code.
If your recent work is advising, configuring, or reviewing rather than writing and shipping code yourself, this role may not be for you.
Wanting a product-only role with no customer contact.
Much of this job is working next to customers, in their environments, on their problems. If you prefer to build away from customers, this role may not be for you.
Inability to earn trust and credibility with partners and customers.
You may be the person who has to explain to a skeptical government security team why our software is safe, or to an internal VP of Engineering why we need to prioritize critical platform features. Those have to be conversations you are willing and excited to have.

Virtruvian qualities that will set you up for success:

Thinking outside of the box to respectfully challenge your teammates and managers in the pursuit of excellence
Strong sense of urgency with an action-oriented mindset
Able to collaborate and adapt to shifting priorities as business needs evolve
Comfortable with asynchronous communication including slack, email, zoom, etc.

Perks & Benefits:

At Virtru, we believe people do their best work when their wellbeing is put first. This is why we make your wellbeing our priority with a thoughtful and holistic program that encompasses Occupational, Mental, Social, Physical, and Environmental Wellness by offering benefits such as…

A Flexible PTO policy — we strongly encourage you to take time off (in addition to 14 holidays) to ensure that you are getting the proper time needed to unplug and recharge.
A $1,500 annual Learning & Development Stipend focused on providing you the resources to continually learn and professionally grow.
Frequent company-sponsored team celebrations that provide ample opportunities to connect with teammates and be social!
Access to an Employee Assistance Program
Access to Headspace, a mental health app tailored to your specific needs.
A flat 3% contribution to your retirement account
A high degree of flexibility
— Have an appointment, errand, or family emergency to take care of? Hop to it! We give you the time and space to take care of you and your own first.

In addition to wellbeing, Virtru places a strong emphasis on diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. Our DB&I Council is dedicated to fostering an inclusive workplace and making the psychological safety of each and every one of our teammates a top priority.

Additional perks include:

Competitive compensation
Generous parental, medical, and bereavement policies
401K contribution and stock options
Full medical, dental, and vision benefits
New Hire Swag and IT Welcome boxes
Structured semi-annual 360° performance reviews

Virtru is committed to building an inclusive environment for people of all backgrounds and everyone is encouraged to apply. Virtru is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, religion, disability, national origin, protected veteran status, age, or any other status protected by applicable national, federal, state, or local law.

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
Forward Deployed Engineer

— Banking Platform

Ship it, then go sit with the people using it.

Charlotte, NC LocationCharlotte, NC — on-site at our headquarters, with travel to partner and client sitesExperience Required5+ years building and shipping production software, including meaningful time in financial services and hands-on experience building with ClaudeEmployment TypeFull-time, exemptReports ToTechnical Program ManagerDirect ReportsNone. You work across engineering, product, operations, and directly with external partners.Core StackReact, Flutter, AWS, GitHub Actions, Claude (Claude Code and the Claude API)PortfolioExpected — see "Show Us Your Work" below The Trade We're Offering We're a smaller institution headquartered in a city full of very large ones, and we're not going to pretend we can match what the largest of them offer on every dimension. What we're offering instead is scope that those jobs structurally cannot give you. At a large bank, this work is split across four teams — a mobile team, a web team, a platform team, and a client-facing integration group — and you'd own a lane in one of them. Here, the whole path from commit to customer is yours. You'll write the Flutter code, write the React code, own the pipeline that ships both, and then sit across the table from the people using what you built and watch where it breaks. Engineers who want that loop rarely get it at scale. If that's the job you've been trying to find, this is it

About The Role

We're hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer to build our banking platform and then take it into the field. This is a hybrid of product engineering and client-facing solutions work: roughly two-thirds building, one-third embedded with the partners, vendors, and internal teams who depend on what you ship.

The forward-deployed part is the point. Most engineering organizations put layers between the person who writes the code and the person who has to live with it, and quality suffers in both directions. You'll close that gap. When an integration fails at a partner, you're the one who diagnoses it — not a support tier that escalates to a queue that eventually reaches engineering three days later.

We also expect this person to be genuinely fluent with Claude — not as a novelty, but as core tooling. A small team competing against institutions a hundred times our size only works if each engineer's output is multiplied. You should already be building this way and be able to show us how.

You'll work closely with the Senior Product Manager who owns the banking portfolio, and you'll have real influence over technical direction. We have opinions but not much legacy, which means your architectural decisions will still be standing in five years.

What You'll Own

Mobile Development — Flutter

Build and ship our customer-facing mobile banking application in Flutter across iOS and Android
Own the release process end to end — store submissions, staged rollouts, versioning, and the deprecation strategy for older clients
Handle the parts of mobile banking that are genuinely hard: biometric authentication, secure local storage, session handling, offline states, and deep links from notifications
Keep performance and app size honest on the low-end devices real customers actually carry

Web Development — React

Build customer-facing web banking experiences and the internal tooling our operations teams use daily
Share logic and design language across web and mobile so the two products don't quietly diverge
Build to accessibility standards — WCAG conformance is a regulatory expectation in consumer banking, not a nice-to-have

Cloud Infrastructure — AWS

Design, deploy, and operate services on AWS — compute, storage, networking, secrets, and identity
Own infrastructure as code so environments are reproducible and auditable rather than hand-assembled
Build for the availability and recovery expectations of a regulated financial institution, and be able to prove them to an examiner
Watch the bill. Cloud cost discipline matters more at our size than it does at a bank that can absorb the waste

Delivery Engineering — GitHub Actions

Own the CI/CD pipelines for web, mobile, and backend services
Build automated testing, security scanning, dependency checks, and deployment gates into the pipeline
Maintain the change controls and audit trail that a regulated environment requires — approvals, artifacts, and release evidence
Make shipping boring. A deployment should be an ordinary Tuesday, not an event

AI-Assisted Engineering — Claude

Use Claude Code as a daily part of how you build — across the codebase, in your IDE, and wired into CI where it earns its place
Hands-on experience building AI-powered product features with the Claude API. You know how to identify high-value use cases (document processing, support workflows, fraud and dispute triage, and internal operations) and build them into reliable production systems
Set the standard for how this team uses AI — what gets automated, what stays human, what gets reviewed before it merges, and what never touches customer data
Write and maintain evaluations for anything AI-driven that reaches production. In banking, "it seemed to work" is not a release criterion
Define the guardrails alongside Risk and Compliance: what data can go to a model, how outputs are logged and reviewed, and how we prove any of it to an examiner

Forward Deployment & Integration

Embed directly with partners, vendors, and internal business teams to deploy, integrate, and troubleshoot in their environment
Own integrations with core banking platforms, payment rails, and fintech APIs — from design through production support
Translate partner needs into implementation plans, building what they actually need (not necessarily what or how they asked)
Bring what you learn in the field back into the roadmap. You'll see the friction before anyone else does, and you're expected to say so

Security, Risk & Compliance

Treat security as a design constraint, not a review stage — encryption in transit and at rest, least privilege, secrets management, secure SDLC
Partner with Risk and Compliance on architecture decisions, vendor assessments, and audit response
Build systems that produce the evidence an examiner will eventually ask for, before they ask for it

What We're Looking For

Required

5+ years building and shipping production software, with real ownership of what you shipped after it launched
Financial services experience. You understand why a banking release is not a social app release — the regulatory constraints, the audit expectations, the consequences of a bad deploy touching real money
Production React experience — modern hooks-based code, state management, and performance work
Production Flutter experience shipping to both app stores, or strong native mobile experience plus a credible case that you'll pick up Flutter fast
Hands-on AWS: you've architected, deployed, and operated services there, not just consumed them
CI/CD ownership with GitHub Actions or a close equivalent (GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins) — you've built pipelines, not just used them
Deep, hands-on Claude experience. You use Claude Code as part of your normal workflow and you've built something real against the Claude API — not a weekend demo, but something with error handling, cost awareness, audit/observability capabilities, and a point of view about when the model should and shouldn't be trusted
Judgment about where AI helps and where it doesn't. We want the engineer who knows which problems to point a model at, and which ones to just write the code for
Client-facing ability. You can sit in a room with a partner's engineering team or a business stakeholder, absorb a vague problem, and leave with a clear scope
Exceptional attention to detail, communication, and documentation. You are precise in your work, clear and direct in how you communicate, and disciplined about documenting decisions, systems, and operational context — especially when working across engineering teams, clients, and partners
Comfort with ambiguity and thin process. You'll frequently be the person who decides how something gets done

Nice to Have — Genuinely Optional

Integration experience with core banking platforms (Fiserv, Jack Henry, FIS, Q2, Alkami, nCino) or payment rails (ACH, Zelle, RTP, FedNow, card networks)
Fintech API work — Plaid, Marqeta, Stripe, Alloy, or similar
Backend depth in Node, Python, Go, Java, or Kotlin
Infrastructure as code (Terraform, CDK, CloudFormation) and containerization
Familiarity with regulatory frameworks touching engineering — SOC 2, PCI DSS, GLBA, FFIEC guidance
Agentic patterns beyond chat — tool use, MCP servers, multi-step workflows, or the Claude Agent SDK
Running Claude models through Amazon Bedrock, which fits neatly with the AWS stack here
Experience writing evals, or any rigorous approach to measuring whether an AI feature actually works
Prior consulting, solutions engineering, or forward-deployed work at a software vendor

If you meet most of the Required list, apply.
The exact stack combination here is uncommon, and we'd rather teach a strong engineer one piece of it than wait for a perfect match who doesn't exist.

Domain Expertise We Value

Domain
Relevant Skills & Tools
MobileFlutter, Dart, iOS & Android release management, biometric auth, secure storageWebReact, TypeScript, modern state management, WCAG accessibilityCloudAWS compute, storage, networking, IAM, infrastructure as codeDeliveryGitHub Actions, automated testing, security scanning, change controlIntegrationCore banking platforms, payment rails, fintech APIs, REST & webhooksAI EngineeringClaude Code, Claude API, tool use and MCP, evaluations, Amazon BedrockRegulated EngineeringSecure SDLC, audit evidence, SOC 2 / PCI DSS / GLBA awareness

What We Can and Can't Offer

What You Get Here
What You Won't Get Here
The full path from commit to customer, owned by one personAnywhere to hide when something you shipped breaksArchitectural decisions that will still be standing in five yearsA platform team that handles infrastructure so you don't have toDirect contact with the people using what you buildInsulation from customers when a deploy goes badlyDeploys in days, not release trains scheduled a quarter outA mature engineering organization with established processGenuine influence on technical direction from your first monthDeep specialization — you'll work across mobile, web, cloud, and AIA mandate to define how a company uses AI, not to inherit someone's rulesAn existing AI platform team, or someone else's guardrails to inheritBudget for conferences, certifications, and continued learningA remote or fully flexible arrangement — this role is on-site

Education

Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience
No degree requirement we'll hold rigidly. Show us what you've shipped. Self-taught engineers with production track records are welcome here
AWS certifications are a plus and are not required

Work Environment

On-site at our Charlotte headquarters, Monday through Friday, standard business hours. Expect periodic travel to partner and client sites — typically a few days at a time, several times a year. Banking platform work occasionally means an evening or a weekend around a release, a core conversion, or an incident. We run a real on-call rotation and we keep it humane.

Show Us Your Work

We ask candidates for this role to share code. A resume tells us where you've been; a repository tells us how you think. Send us one or two repositories you've built
— ideally something involving Claude, a mobile or web application, or infrastructure you're proud of. Personal projects, open-source contributions, and side work all count.

If your best work is proprietary, that is not a disqualifier.
Most engineers coming out of financial services cannot share what they built, and we're not going to penalize you for honoring an agreemen

The business result the client is paying for, from ambiguous first conversation to production system.

To the client, when the scope is wrong or the timeline is fiction.

Has sat across the table from a client's engineering, security, and compliance teams simultaneously, and gotten to yes.

You own an outcome, not a backlog assigned by a client PM.

You ship production code. If the engagement doesn't produce shipped software, it doesn't count.

You'll work across Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, SpaceXAI, and NVIDIA stacks depending on what the client's problem requires — not a single-platform mandate.

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
Why This Role

Concourse is building the operating system for State and Local governments. Our platform is a configurable approach to tackling fragmented government data and workflows, turning them into smooth operations for public servants and the constituents they serve. Every product we ship (e.g., school-district IT helpdesk, city-wide ERP, county-wide bail management system) is configured and customized by a Forward-Deployed team, ensuring the final-mile delivery of our software is relevant to our customers’ workflows.

You're the technical horsepower to a forward deployed PM paired with you on every project. That means rolling up your sleeves on the data models, workflows, and components (built as reusable scaffolding instead of a one-off), while the PM leans into customer solutioning alongside you. You’re extending and hardening our platform’s scaffolding against a new customer's specific requirements.

Our platform engineers hand you the connectors, workflow engine, and low-level primitives that everything is built on. You sit in the layer above that, building and continuously improving the product-type scaffolding that every FDPM you work with will reuse.

Government workflows are messy and legacy systems fight you at every turn. What you build here compounds.

What You'll Do

Pair with an FDPM on every project for a given product category, from the first build through every deployment after it
On a new product type, design and build the components, data models, and workflows as reusable scaffolding
On later deployments of a product type, extend and harden that scaffolding against each new customer's specific data and edge cases, while the FDPM handles configuration and finishing touches
Get your hands dirty with real government data: legacy exports, mainframe extracts, undocumented APIs, and the inevitable exceptions that come with it
Use AI coding tools to build and iterate quickly, shipping working modules against a live customer instead of a backlog
Feed what you learn about the platform's gaps back to the Platform Engineering team so the lower-level primitives improve with every product category you build

What We're Looking For

A portfolio: what have you built end-to-end, from scratch, under pressure?
Strong backend fluency, with good instincts for abstraction: knowing what to generalize into reusable scaffolding vs. what to leave specific to one customer
Enough frontend ability to build and ship a usable UI without needing to hand it off
Hands-on experience using AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Factory, etc.) as a core part of your daily workflow
Comfort working directly with non-technical stakeholders alongside an FDPM, even if you're not the one owning the relationship
High-agency, high-velocity mindset: comfortable being the first engineer into a brand-new product category, and just as comfortable staying paired in on every deployment after it
US citizen (required for government work)
Willing to work in-person in Flatiron, NYC (5 days/week)

Nice to have:
experience building internal tooling, developer platforms, or reusable component libraries; prior startup experience shipping directly to customers; public sector domain knowledge (courts, permitting, utilities, school districts); or experience working with legacy/mainframe data.

About Concourse

Concourse is the fastest-growing govtech, providing software to more than 100 state and local governments across the U.S.

Government calls what we do "IT modernization." We call it a trillion-dollar opportunity to overhaul how government works. Public services are broken not because of bureaucracy but instead because they run on antiquated, user-unfriendly software from legacy vendors.

Some examples: Concourse is powering the legislative management system for one of America's largest cities, a state's entire online bail payment system, and a case-management platform for mental-health response teams.

We are an AI-native company. Our org structure and staffing model are radically different from those of legacy tech companies: we have a flat team of superstar generalists who both own client relationships and manage fleets of long-horizon AI agents.

Our team works together in our Flatiron office five days a week.

Compensation Range: $140K - $190K

added.title: Forward Deployed AI Engineer
added.description:
When you join Verizon

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. At Verizon, we power and empower how people live, work and play by connecting them to what brings them joy. We do what we love — driving innovation, creativity, and impact in the world. Our V Team is a community of people who anticipate, lead, and believe that listening is where learning begins. In crisis and in celebration, we come together — lifting our communities and building trust in how we show up, everywhere & always. Want in? Join the #VTeamLife.

What You’ll Be Doing...

As a Forward Deployed AI Engineer within Verizon’s Transformation Command Center (TCC), you will embed directly into the frontline of Verizon’s core Business Units to solve our most critical, ambiguous, and high-stakes operational challenges. Operating with technical ownership, you will help to architect, build, and deploy production-grade agentic systems, enterprise RAG engines, full-stack microservices, and decision systems into live operations.

You are a technical anchor; you pair deep systems craftsmanship with a product mindset, cutting through operational ambiguity to design production architectures, implement custom orchestration layers (via LangGraph, Temporal, or custom state machines), and enforce context management strategies that scale into enterprise assets. Beyond shipping point solutions, you will run workloads reliably on Domino, Airflow, and Kubernetes, abstracting bespoke code into reusable SDKs, shared libraries, and architectural playbooks that scale company-wide.

Key Responsibilities Include

End-to-End Architectural Understanding: Utilizing the full-stack architecture for embedded AI initiatives, including multi-agent orchestration, state machines, latency/cost budgets, security boundaries, and enterprise back-end integrations.
Agentic Orchestration Engineering, Workflow Automation and Governance: Implementing stateful agent workflows complying with established agentic governance rules, using tools like LangGraph, Temporal, or event-driven state machines, establishing strict protocols for tool calling, execution sandboxing, and deterministic fallback logic.
Context & Retrieval Systems: Designing production RAG infrastructure incorporating hybrid search, re-ranking algorithms, metadata filtering, and semantic caching, directly informing and scaling Verizon’s context architecture.
Runtime & Cloud Deployment: Deploying production agent services and scheduled workflows to target runtimes (e.g., Domino Data Lab, Apache Airflow, Kubernetes microservices, and serverless compute across AWS, GCP, or Azure).
Evaluation Harness Design: Architecting offline and online evaluation frameworks (e.g., LLM-as-a-judge, synthetic test generation, human-in-the-loop review queues, live A/B rollouts) to measure model drift, context hallucination rates, and task completion metrics.
Platform Codification: Generalizing custom domain deployments into reusable internal SDKs, API primitives, and modular UI components.
Strategic Discovery & Scoping: Embed alongside BU leadership to map intricate operational processes, cut through organizational noise, and isolate the highest-leverage intervention points where applied AI delivers measurable uplift.
Executive Translation: Serving as a technical engineer in the room with Directors and above, demystifying algorithmic behaviors, failure modes, and performance trade-offs.

What We’re Looking For...

You’ll need to have:

Bachelor’s degree or four or more years of work experience.
Four or more years of relevant experience required, demonstrated through work experience and/or military experience.
Extensive hands-on experience leveraging frontier LLMs (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini) and agentic developer frameworks (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to build scalable solutions and achieve core business milestones.
A strong foundation in statistics and machine learning, applied to problems such as forecasting, prioritization, or optimization.
Strong proficiency in Python and modern TypeScript/Node.js for full-stack API integration and backend orchestration.
Experience with containerized deployments (Docker), API design, and cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure).
Proven track record implementing both offline evaluation benchmarks and online evaluation/observability pipelines (latency, token costs, hallucination tracking, eval-driven development).
Proven experience deploying containerized services and data workflows across enterprise platforms such as Domino Data Lab, Apache Airflow, Kubernetes (EKS/GKE), and hyperscaler cloud environments (AWS/GCP/Azure).
Proven track record designing offline/online eval harnesses, guardrail frameworks, and observability systems (latency, token optimization, tracing).
Demonstrated ability to interface directly with enterprise stakeholders, translate ambiguous business requirements into technical architectures, and lead project delivery end-to-end.

Even Better If You Have

Bachelor or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related technical field.
Experience building and scaling centralized context platforms or enterprise search engines similar to Verizon's internal enterprise context layer platforms.
Three or more years shipping production software and/or demonstrated experience deploying LLM applications, agentic workflows, or autonomous tool-calling pipelines into production.
Demonstrated ability to independently scope ambiguous technical initiatives and present architectural designs to senior executive stakeholders.
Prior forward-deployed engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting experience in top-tier technology firms or hyperscalers.
Record of turning one-off operational builds into enterprise-wide shared libraries, with associated technical publications or filed patents.
Domain knowledge in telecommunications, network capacity optimization, capital planning, or large-scale customer care operations.
Deep expertise in retrieval and context architectures: designing production RAG pipelines, vector databases (e.g., pgvector, Milvus, Pinecone), hybrid search (dense + sparse/lexical), and dynamic context management.
Advanced full-stack programming mastery in Python, SQL, and modern JavaScript/TypeScript stacks.
Demonstrated experience designing, building, validating, and deploying machine learning models for time series forecasting and analysis, including statistical methods (ARIMA/SARIMA, exponential smoothing, Prophet) and ML/deep learning approaches (gradient boosting such as XGBoost/LightGBM, LSTM, or transformer-based models).
Proficient in time series feature engineering (lags, rolling windows, seasonality, holiday and event effects), handling missing data, outliers, and structural breaks, and applying backtesting and cross-validation methods suited to temporal data.
Able to quantify forecast uncertainty with prediction intervals and scenario ranges, evaluate accuracy using metrics such as MAPE, RMSE, and MASE, and monitor deployed models for drift.

If Verizon and this role sound like a fit for you, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every “even better” qualification listed above.

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

Join a team of 10 within Salesforce AI Labs, bringing computer-use AI into production with the autonomy of a small startup and the reach of Salesforce. We’re building Systems Integration Agent, announced at Dreamforce, which learns how to operate enterprise applications and turns complex workflows into reusable, code-backed automation. Customers are already running workflows in production; now we’re making that success repeatable across more systems and use cases.

Making computer use dependable raises hard engineering questions. How does an agent know it succeeded? When should it reason, and when should it follow a deterministic path? How should it recover when an application changes or ask for help before making a consequential mistake?

You’ll help answer those questions in production. Our team works directly with customers, building alongside them and turning discoveries into reusable product capabilities. As a Principal Engineer, you’ll remain hands-on while shaping architecture across our agent and backend systems, owning critical capabilities from design through operation, and helping other engineers deliver them.

Drive Agent Development & Architecture

Design and build systems that learn from demonstrations and combine AI reasoning with deterministic execution to complete workflows reliably.
Develop recovery and verification capabilities so agents can adapt to changes, confirm outcomes, and recognize when human intervention is needed.
Build backend services with robust workflow state management, failure handling, and secure access to customer environments.
Create evaluations and diagnostics that measure task success, expose regressions, and make failures understandable.

Build Directly With Customers

Work alongside customers to understand their workflows, prototype solutions, and validate results in their environments.
Investigate where automation succeeds or fails, then turn those findings into improvements to the core product.
Help customers move from their first successful workflow toward repeatable, increasingly self-service adoption.
Partner with forward-deployed engineers and product management to decide which customer needs should shape the roadmap.

Shape Technical Direction & Grow the Team

Evaluate model selection, tool use, and context management against reliability, latency, and cost.
Raise the engineering bar through hands-on implementation, design reviews, and mentoring; help engineers take on broader ownership and participate in hiring.

You’ve led the architecture and delivery of complex backend systems through deployment, production failures, and subsequent improvements, with impact across multiple components or teams.

You’re proficient in Python, Go, Java, or JavaScript/TypeScript.
You can turn an unclear customer problem into a bounded technical approach, test it with users, and lead it through production while creating capabilities other engineers can build on.
You want direct customer engagement to be part of your engineering work, including investigating problems and discussing technical tradeoffs.
You use AI development tools thoughtfully and take responsibility for the correctness, security, and maintainability of what you ship.

Agent tool use, code generation, automated recovery, or evaluation frameworks.
Browser automation, workflow orchestration, or enterprise integrations.
Building an early-stage product or working in a customer-facing engineering role.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Applications will be accepted until 01/01/2027.

The Experience

We are seeking a Senior Member of Technical Staff to design, build, and ship autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents integrated with our platform. In this role, you will work at the intersection of LLM orchestration, tool-use frameworks, and production engineering—turning agentic prototypes into reliable, scalable, enterprise-grade systems. As a recognized SME and hybrid engineer, you will own complex functionality from end-to-end design to delivery and operation, while guiding team execution and quality standards.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Agentic Systems Engineering: Design, build, and deploy multi-step, tool-using AI agents (planning, reasoning, memory, tool invocation) and integrate them with APIs, databases, and enterprise systems (e.g., Salesforce, Slack).
Architecture & Orchestration: Evaluate and select agent frameworks/orchestration patterns (ReAct, planner-executor, multi-agent, etc.) and optimize deployments for latency, cost, and production reliability.
Agile Execution & Technical Delivery: Independently deliver high-quality, complex features across the entire lifecycle (design, execution, testing, review). Assist in slicing epics, defining tasks, and managing dependencies alongside PMs and Scrum Masters.
Guardrails, Monitoring & Operations: Build robust evaluation harnesses and guardrails to prevent hallucinations, drift, and unsafe tool calls. Proactively monitor features in production, lead incident handling (TTx), and contribute to PRBs/RCAs.
Leadership & Collaboration: Act as a SME and technical coach for AMTS/MTS engineers via pair programming and reviews. Present planned and delivered work to leadership and technical audiences, and partner with Tech Writers on documentation.

You're Our Person If

Experience: 4+ years of software engineering experience, including hands-on experience building and deploying LLMs/agentic systems in production environments.
Technical Proficiency: Strong Python skills with mastery of agent orchestration frameworks (e.g., LangGraph, AutoGen, custom frameworks) or ability to construct frameworks from scratch.
AI Concepts: Deep understanding of prompt engineering, tool-calling/function-calling patterns, RAG, and evaluation strategies for non-deterministic systems.
Systems & Architecture: Solid expertise in API integrations, async systems, distributed architectures, and modern software design patterns.
Communication & Leadership: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of cross-functional alignment, technical coaching, and constructive code reviews.

Even Better If

Experience with enterprise SaaS architectures, the Salesforce ecosystem, multi-agent coordination, or emerging protocols like MCP.

LI-Y*

added.title: Sr AI Software Engineer
added.description:
The Trade Desk is a global technology company and the world’s leading independent platform for digital advertising, with over 3,000 employees across more than 30 offices. Our technology helps advertisers reach the right audiences across the open internet — from streaming TV and podcasts to mobile apps, news, and more.

Advertising powers the content people love. By making it more transparent, effective, and responsible, we help support trusted journalism, quality entertainment, and creators worldwide. The world’s brands and agencies rely on us to reach their customers and grow their businesses responsibly.

The scale of our platform brings unique technical challenges — from processing massive datasets in real time to building systems that operate reliably on a global scale. When you work here, your impact is worldwide. We welcome diverse perspectives, encourage curiosity, and build teams that learn from one another. If you’re driven to solve meaningful challenges, we’d love to meet you.

What we do:

You’ll join a software engineering team that builds internal AI solutions supporting teams across The Trade Desk. We use large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic systems, custom MCP servers, and enterprise platforms like Anthropic Claude to improve productivity, streamline workflows, and reduce operational friction.

Our team also plays a key role in AI enablement across the company—supporting teams as they adopt Copilot, Claude and similar tools, designing and deploying custom AI agents, and guiding partners through their AI journey from idea to impact.

As a Senior AI Software Engineer on this team, you’ll be an end-to-end owner—collaborating closely with stakeholders, identifying opportunities, and delivering tools that make a real impact. We’re a nimble, fast-paced, and highly collaborative group that thrives on transforming the way teams operate and driving greater value across The Trade Desk.

What you'll do:

Some of the work that you will be doing to help us deliver on our mission is:

Partner with Business teams across The Trade Desk to understand Business processes, identify opportunities, scope and prioritize use cases, and define success metrics before building.
Design and build agents and agentic workflows, including background and conversational agents, that orchestrate tools, data, and business processes end to end to solve real-world problems and deliver measurable business value within enterprise guardrails.
Design and build custom MCP servers that securely expose enterprise data, APIs, and internal systems to AI agents, with well-designed tool schemas, proper authentication, least-privilege permission scoping, and observability.
Design and deploy intelligent agentic systems that integrate large language models (LLMs) with enterprise data, tools, and workflows using modern agent SDKs and orchestration frameworks.
Rapidly prototype, validate with real users, then harden the winners into supported solutions or hand them off to the owning team.
Drive adoption through training, office hours, playbooks, reusable templates, and reference implementations that other teams can self-serve from.
Drive quality and performance through automated testing, evaluation suites, monitoring, and data-driven evaluation of success criteria, user adoption, cost, and operational efficiency.
Mentor teammates and contribute to a culture of innovation, technical excellence, and continuous learning.

Who you are:

You have a Bachelor's/Master's level degree in computer science or relevant engineering-related field or equivalent experience.
You have 6-8+ years of experience in software engineering, forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, or technical consulting, including 1-2+ years building LLM-powered solutions that reached real users in production.
You are proficient in Python and/or TypeScript and comfortable with additional languages such as C# or SQL.
You're excited about AI, including helping teams adopt Anthropic Claude, building agents, workflows and MCP servers, and guiding others through their AI journey.
You have hands-on experience with LLM APIs, tool use, and prompt engineering, and you've built MCP servers or equivalent function-calling integrations, or can show you'd ramp up quickly.
You have experience with enterprise identity and access, including OAuth, SSO/Entra ID, and scoping permissions so an agent can only do what the user is allowed to do.
You have experience productionizing applications and implementing CI/CD pipelines to ensure reliable, scalable deployments.
You are skilled in data ingestion and transformation using APIs, ETL pipelines, and connectors, and familiar with vector databases and retrieval strategies.
You treat evaluation and safety as core engineering work, including evals, tracing, prompt-injection defenses, and cost and latency management.
You communicate clearly across technical and non-technical audiences, can run discovery sessions and demos with business partners, and thrive in a collaborative, cross-functional environment.
You are a fast learner who adapts quickly to new technologies and solves complex problems with creativity and pragmatism.

added.description:
Be the one building AI-powered experiences where they matter most.

At Genesys, we help organizations create better customer experiences through AI-powered experience orchestration. Our platform connects people, systems, data and AI to help organizations deliver more personalized service, improve operational efficiency and build stronger customer relationships.

Help build, support and operate technology used by more than 8,000 organizations in over 100 countries – moving AI from possibility to production in real-world enterprise environments every day.

AI Forward Deployed Engineer

LOCATION

US or Canada - Remote

U.S. LOCATIONS
MAY INCLUDE

Indianapolis, IN; Arizona; Colorado; Michigan; North Carolina; Ohio; Texas; Virginia

Role Overview

The AI Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) is the technical owner for strategic customer AI engagements, responsible for turning high-value business problems into working, production-ready AI solutions. This role sits at the intersection of business strategy, AI engineering, solution architecture, and hands-on delivery. The FDE works directly with customer business and technical teams to identify the right problem, rapidly build and validate a solution, deploy it into real operating environments, and continuously optimize it against measurable business outcomes.

This is a builder role. Success requires equal comfort with executive discovery, architecture whiteboarding, writing and debugging code, integrating enterprise systems and data, evaluating agent behavior, and resolving blockers with Product and Engineering. The FDE maintains end-to-end accountability from discovery through production and converts lessons from each engagement into reusable assets that accelerate the next customer.

Key Responsibilities

Own customer outcomes end to end. Partner with customer business and technical leaders to identify and prioritize high-value AI use cases, define measurable success criteria, and own the technical outcome from discovery through prototype, live test, production, and optimization.
Build hands-on. Rapidly prototype, code, configure, integrate, test, and deploy AI solutions using customer systems, APIs, data, workflows, and cloud services.
Engineer agentic AI systems. Design and optimize agent behavior, prompts, context, tool invocation, orchestration, grounding, retrieval, memory, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop patterns.
Connect AI to the enterprise. Develop secure integrations across APIs, webhooks, enterprise applications, data platforms, identity systems, and legacy environments so AI agents can act reliably within real business workflows.
Validate with engineering rigor. Build evaluation and observability approaches that test accuracy, safety, latency, reliability, and business outcomes; diagnose failures and edge cases and iterate rapidly.
Move prototypes into production. Apply sound software engineering, security, governance, CI/CD, version control, monitoring, and operational practices to deliver maintainable production solutions.
Remove production blockers. Work directly with Genesys Product, Engineering, Support, and cross-functional teams to identify platform gaps, resolve technical issues, and unblock customer deployment.
Co-build with customers. Work alongside customer engineers and architects, transfer knowledge, and leave customer teams more capable of operating and extending the solution after the engagement.
Create the field-to-product feedback loop. Translate repeatable customer needs, deployment friction, and edge cases into actionable product feedback, feature requests, technical patterns, and reference implementations.
Build once, scale everywhere. Package proven agents, integrations, prompts, evaluation methods, deployment patterns, and implementation playbooks into reusable assets that accelerate future customer engagements.
Operate with ownership and urgency. Maintain accountability through resolution, manage ambiguity, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and drive multiple stakeholders toward measurable outcomes.

Required Qualifications

8+ years of relevant technical experience in software engineering, AI engineering, solutions engineering, technical delivery, solution architecture, or a comparable hands-on role; equivalent practical experience will be considered.
Demonstrated production ownership. Experience taking at least one meaningful software, AI, data, or integration solution from concept or prototype into a production environment and supporting it through real-world use.
Enterprise integration expertise. Experience designing or building with REST APIs, webhooks, authentication/authorization, structured and unstructured data, and modern cloud or SaaS architectures.
Applied AI and LLM knowledge. Practical experience with large language models and agentic AI concepts such as prompt and context engineering, tool/function calling, orchestration, grounding, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), evaluation, and guardrails.
Engineering discipline for AI. Ability to test, debug, monitor, and improve AI systems using repeatable evaluation, tracing, logging, versioning, and software quality practices.
Customer-facing technical leadership. Ability to lead discovery and technical working sessions, translate ambiguous business problems into buildable technical solutions, and communicate credibly with both senior executives and engineers.
High-agency execution. A record of learning quickly, making sound tradeoffs, operating effectively with incomplete information, and owning problems through resolution rather than handing them off.
Collaborative product mindset. Ability to work across Sales, Solution Consulting, Product, Engineering, Support, Security, and customer teams while converting field learnings into reusable patterns and product feedback.
AI-native development mindset. Comfort using modern AI-assisted development tools and coding agents to accelerate software delivery while remaining accountable for code quality, security, and maintainability.
AI-assisted engineering tools. Experience using tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Amazon Kiro, or similar AI coding environments as part of a regular development workflow.
Enterprise data and knowledge systems. Experience with vector databases, search, data pipelines, knowledge retrieval, enterprise data platforms, or integrating AI with CRM, ERP, ITSM, or other systems of record.
Agentic AI experience. Hands-on experience building multi-agent systems, tool-using agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, agent-to-agent workflows, or orchestration frameworks such as LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, CrewAI, LangChain, or LlamaIndex.
Travel flexibility. Ability to travel to customer sites and company events as needed for strategic engagements.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on programming capability. Strong proficiency in at least one modern programming language such as Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or an equivalent language, with the ability and willingness to learn additional technologies quickly.
Production AI observability and optimization. Experience with evaluation pipelines, tracing, latency and cost optimization, reliability monitoring, safety controls, or LLM-native performance metrics.
Cloud and deployment experience. Experience with AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud and with deployment technologies such as Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, or serverless architectures.
Conversational or voice AI experience. Experience building customer-facing conversational AI, virtual agents, voice AI, or contact-center solutions.
Customer experience domain knowledge. Experience with Genesys Cloud CX, customer experience technology, contact center platforms, workforce engagement, routing, or related enterprise SaaS solutions is valuable but not required.
Security and responsible AI. Understanding of enterprise security, identity and access management, data privacy, auditability, permissioning, prompt injection risks, and safe tool execution for AI systems.
Education. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Data Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced technical education is a plus but not required.

The profile we are building:
Business thinker. Hands-on builder. Customer technologist. Relentless owner. Builds once, scales everywhere.

Compensation:

This role has a market-competitive salary with an anticipated base compensation range listed below. Actual salaries will vary depending on a candidate’s experience, qualifications, skills, and location. This role might also be eligible for a commission or performance-based bonus opportunities.

Our platform connects to thousands of financial institutions, powering use cases from account verification to risk assessment to personal financial management. Across the Financial Connections Engineering org, we focus on delivering high-quality, enriched bank data at scale — building the ML systems that transform raw financial data into actionable signals for both internal Stripe teams and external merchants.

Our ML work spans transaction categorization, risk scoring, data enrichment, and the development of intelligent systems that improve data quality across our network. We operate at the intersection of fintech infrastructure and applied machine learning, solving problems that directly impact Stripe's ability to serve millions of businesses and consumers.

What you'll do

We're looking for machine learning engineers who want to build intelligent systems that provide financial data at scale. You'll play a key role in designing, training, and deploying ML models that improve the quality, accuracy, and usefulness of financial data across Stripe's ecosystem.

Responsibilities

Design, build, train, evaluate, deploy, and own ML models in production that improve transaction categorization, risk scoring, and data enrichment across Financial Connections
Design and build large-scale ML systems that operate on diverse financial data from thousands of institutions
Experiment and iterate on ML models (using tools such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost) to achieve key business goals around data quality and accuracy
Develop pipelines and automated processes to train and evaluate models in offline and online environments
Integrate ML models into production systems and ensure their scalability and reliability
Collaborate with product, data science, and engineering partners across Stripe to identify opportunities where ML can improve outcomes for merchants and consumers
Engage with the latest ML/AI developments and take calculated risks in transforming innovative ideas into productionized solutions
Mentor engineers and contribute to a strong ML engineering culture within the team

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

10+ years of industry experience building and shipping ML systems in production
Proficient with ML libraries and frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost, as well as Spark
Hands-on experience in designing, training, and evaluating machine learning models
Hands-on experience in productionizing and deploying models at scale
Hands-on experience in orchestrating data pipelines and efficiently leveraging large-scale datasets
Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work across teams and contribute to peers' success
Ability to thrive with a high level of autonomy and responsibility and an entrepreneurial mindset

Preferred Qualifications

MS or PhD degree in ML/AI or a related field (e.g., math, physics, statistics, computer science)
Experience in fintech, open banking, or financial data domains
Experience with NLP, LLMs, or text classification at scale
Experience in adversarial or noisy-data domains such as fraud detection, risk modeling, or data quality
Proven track record of building and deploying ML systems that have effectively solved ambiguous business problems
Experience with deep learning architectures, including transformers

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $253,500 - $380,300. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

added.title: Member of Technical Staff, AI
added.description:
Drug development shouldn’t be guesswork, not when patients are waiting.

Pathos is building a next-generation biotech with AI at the core. Not as a feature, but as the operating system for how medicines get developed. We believe most drugs don't fail because the science was wrong. They fail because they were tested in the wrong patients, with the wrong assumptions, in trials that couldn't answer the real question: who benefits, and why?

Pathos exists to change that. We're building the largest foundation model in oncology and pairing it with proprietary AI systems, deep oncology expertise, and 200+ petabytes of multimodal data linked to patient outcomes, so we can make development decisions with more precision, much earlier.

This is not theoretical. We’re well-capitalized and have the leadership to build a generational company. We invest in and advance our own clinical-stage programs, using our AI platform to sharpen trial design, patient selection and biomarker strategy. So therapies reach the patients most likely to benefit, sooner.

How We Build

Pathos does not operate like a traditional biotech. There is no middle management. There are no layers of approval. The company is designed, from the ground up, around small teams of 2–4 subject matter experts who each command hundreds of AI agents to do the work that used to require dozens of people.

Everyone builds. Everyone ships. Every function at Pathos — from clinical execution to asset selection to the foundation model itself — runs on this model. Our product velocity delivers meaningful outcomes in hours instead of weeks. This is not a future aspiration. It is how we operate today.

The people who thrive here are operators: deep experts who can specify what needs to happen, orchestrate AI agents to execute at scale, and make high-judgment calls that compound over time. If you have spent your career building and shipping AI systems at scale, this is the environment where that experience becomes a superpower.

About The Role

Applications will be reviewed continuously, with priority consideration for submissions received by December 7, 2026.

You will play a major role in advancing the foundation model and building the agentic systems behind Foundry, the AI platform that informs every drug decision at Pathos, and make them continually improve over time from real-world feedback.

You will own how we train and adapt frontier open-weight models specifically for drug development. You will leverage 200+ petabytes of multimodal, multi-scale oncology data spanning over 8 million patient records linked to longitudinal outcomes, alongside live data streams from clinical trial sites. Supported by a dedicated large-scale GPU cluster and our internal wet lab for experimental validation, your models will directly inform design and execution of clinical trials. You will operate within a lean, high-velocity team where every builder maintains end-to-end ownership over key platform capabilities.

If you want to build the intelligence behind how new medicines are developed, and prove rigorously that it gets better, this is the place to do your career’s best work.

What You’ll Build

Advance mid- and post-training of our oncology foundation model across SFT and RL, including reward design and verifiers for scientific and clinical tasks whose correctness is hard to check automatically.
Run and debug training at scale, addressing instability, divergence and reward hacking.
Build the harness for scientific and clinical workflows: memory, context management, orchestration and tools, plus methods that optimize the harness automatically and evolve it together with the underlying model.
Design evaluations for open-ended, long-horizon scientific, clinical and operational tasks, calibrate them against expert judgment, investigate where they fail, and use them to decide what ships.
Build pipelines that generate, filter and curate training and evaluation data, with safeguards for quality, provenance and contamination.
Turn expert feedback, wet-lab results and real-time signals from clinical trial sites into improvements to models, harness and evaluations, so the platform learns from experience with very high sample efficiency.
Work directly with oncologists, biologists and the clinical team to translate drug development needs into tractable ML problems, and publish in top ML and scientific venues.

Who You Are

We’re looking for researchers and engineers who have gotten models or agents working at scale, care as much about the drugs as about the models, and want their work to reach patients. You take ambiguous problems through experiments to results people can use.

We’re hiring across levels, from exceptional early-career talent to experienced researchers.

Must-haves

Deep, hands-on expertise in at least one of the following, which we value equally:

Mid- or post-training at scale, such as SFT, RL, reward modeling or preference optimization, with direct ownership of training runs and results.
Evaluation, data and agent harness design, such as evaluation and feedback design for scientific, clinical and operational tasks, synthetic data pipelines, or harness optimization spanning memory, context management, orchestration and tools.

Rigorous scientific judgment, including when ground truth is limited, delayed or disputed.
Strong engineering skills in Python, with production-quality code.
Clear communication of evidence, limitations and uncertainty.
Willingness to learn biology and drug development, and work closely with domain experts.

Publications, research software and deployed systems are all valid evidence. Publications are welcome but not required.

Bonus

You’ve built self-improving agentic systems, for example through self-play, synthetic data generation, self-training on past trajectories or test-time learning, or systems that automate ML research.
You’ve built AI systems for real-world scientific workflows, such as agents that generate hypotheses and design, run and analyze experiments using lab or clinical data.
You’ve built RL environments or task suites for training agents on realistic, long-horizon tasks.
You’ve modeled multimodal biomedical data, such as genomics, transcriptomics, pathology and radiology images, clinical notes and EHRs, ideally combining several modalities in one model.
You’ve worked on uncertainty estimation, calibration or causal inference, especially where model outputs inform high-stakes decisions.
You’ve built or scaled infrastructure for efficient training and inference, such as distributed training, custom kernels (CUDA or Triton) or high-throughput serving.
You’ve shipped ML systems that real users rely on, then monitored them in production and improved them from user feedback.
You have a background in oncology, drug development or clinical research, or a track record of working closely with clinicians and biologists.
You’ve worked with patient-level or clinical trial data under privacy and regulatory constraints, such as HIPAA.

None of these are required. We value depth in one area over breadth across all of them.

Location

The preferred location for this position is in our New York City HQ, though exceptional remote candidates will also be considered.

Compensation

We are hiring across levels. The anticipated salary range is $220,000 to $350,000 plus equity, and we have flexibility for exceptional candidates.

added.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Prime Video - Ads Science
added.description:
Description

Prime Video is a first-stop entertainment destination offering customers a vast collection of premium programming in one app available across thousands of devices. Prime members can customize their viewing experience and find their favorite movies, series, documentaries, and live sports – including Amazon MGM Studios-produced series and movies; licensed fan favorites; and programming from Prime Video subscriptions such as Apple TV+, HBO Max, Peacock, Crunchyroll and MGM+. All customers, regardless of whether they have a Prime membership or not, can rent or buy titles via the Prime Video Store, and can enjoy even more content for free with ads.

Are you interested in shaping the future of entertainment? Prime Video's technology teams are creating best-in-class digital video experience.

As a Prime Video team member, you’ll have end-to-end ownership of the product, user experience, design, and technology required to deliver state-of-the-art experiences for our customers. You’ll get to work on projects that are fast-paced, challenging, and varied. You’ll also be able to experiment with new possibilities, take risks, and collaborate with remarkable people.

We’ll look for you to bring your diverse perspectives, ideas, and skill-sets to make Prime Video even better for our customers. With global opportunities for talented technologists, you can decide where a career Prime Video Tech takes you!

Key job responsibilities

The Science Challenges Include

Heterogeneous customer responses. The same customer responds differently to ads depending on what they’re watching, how engaged they are, and their broader streaming context. We need to understand and predict this variation to make better advertising decisions in real time.
Signal sparsity in streaming. Unlike search or retail advertising, streaming offers no clicks, no conversions, and limited direct feedback. We must develop creative approaches to infer customer preferences, intent, and tolerance from indirect behavioral signals.
Personalization at scale. A one-size-fits-all ad experience leaves value on the table for both customers and the business. We build systems that adapt ad load, placement, and content to individual viewers across 100M+ customers and 100k+ titles.
Small effects, large variance. Ad interventions typically produce 0.1-2% shifts in engagement, effects easily overwhelmed by natural behavioral variance. Measuring, attributing, and optimizing these small signals requires rigorous experimental design and causal methodologies.
Competing objectives. Revenue, customer engagement, long-term retention, and advertiser value are in tension. We develop principled frameworks to navigate these tradeoffs and optimize for sustainable outcomes rather than any single metric.

A day in the life

Lead the research and development of ML models that personalize advertising decisions for 100M+ customers across 100k+ titles, with production deployment in mind
Develop deep learning architectures (multi-task learning, embedding-based representations) for customer behavior prediction at scale
Design and analyze large-scale A/B experiments, applying causal inference techniques to measure and optimize the impact of ad strategies on customer engagement and monetization
Partner with engineering to ensure models meet production latency and scalability requirements
Collaborate with product managers to frame business problems as tractable ML problems and translate findings into product decisions
Shape the team’s scientific roadmap, identifying high-impact research directions

About The Team

Prime Video Ads is pioneering the use of Generative AI, Deep Learning and Causal ML to empower the next generation of Ads experience in Prime Video. Our vision is to build the world’s most valuable and differentiated ad-supported streaming platform: one where every ad is relevant to the viewer, and every dollar spent by an advertiser delivers measurable results. We are seeking lead applied scientists who have demonstrated experience in advancing state of the art ML algorithms, particularly in Personalization, Relevance, Casual Inference and Gen-AI areas. Your role will be to deliver these innovations as production-ready systems at Amazon scale.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of building machine learning models for business application experience
PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with large scale machine learning systems such as profiling and debugging and understanding of system performance and scalability

added.description:
About ETS

ETS is a global education and talent solutions organization enabling lifelong learners worldwide to be future-ready. For more than 80 years, we've been advancing the science of measurement to build benchmarks for fair and valid skill assessment across cultures and borders. Our worldwide impact extends through our renowned assessments including TOEFL®, TOEIC®, GRE® and Praxis® tests, serving millions of learners in more than 200 countries and territories. Through strategic acquisitions, we've expanded our global capabilities: PSI strengthens our workforce assessment solutions, ACT solidifies our impact in higher Ed and Workskills while Edusoft enhances our educational technology and assessment platforms across critical markets worldwide.

Through ETS Research Institute and ETS Solutions, we're partnering with educational institutions, governments, and organizations globally to promote skill proficiency, empower upward mobility, and unlock opportunities for everyone, everywhere. With offices and partners across Asia, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas, we deliver nearly 50 million tests annually. Join us in our journey of measuring progress to power human progress worldwide.

The ETS Research Institute's Center for Responsible AI for Learning and Assessment studies how AI can improve learning and assessment, and how we can validly measure what a person knows and can do when AI is part of the learning, the task, or the scoring. The Center's research includes AI-enabled interactive assessments, the measurement of AI literacy, personalized assessment, and the responsible use of AI in scoring and test development. Our scientists include learning scientists, cognitive psychologists, statisticians, psychometricians, computational linguists, and research engineers. We are seeking a colleague whose expertise in artificial intelligence, machine learning, or statistics will complement theirs.

We Welcome Applicants From a Wide Range Of Quantitative Fields. Areas Of Particular Interest Include, But Are Not Limited To, The Following

AI for learning and assessment: developing AI systems such as tutors, feedback tools, and conversational agents, with attention to how well they work and for whom.
Evaluations and benchmarks of AI in education: methods for evaluating AI systems used in teaching, learning, and assessment, including benchmark design, validation of automated judgments against human ratings, and analyses of reliability and fairness.
Causal evidence and statistics: experimental, quasi-experimental, and statistical methods that estimate the effects of AI tools on learners and teachers, or that strengthen inferences from complex data.

We do not expect applicants to work in all of these areas, and we encourage applications from people whose work in AI, machine learning, or statistics connects to learning and assessment in other ways.

Primary Responsibilities

Conduct and publish rigorous research on AI in learning and assessment, drawing on methods from machine learning, statistics, and measurement.
Collaborate with learning scientists, psychometricians, and research engineers on projects across the Center, contributing AI and statistical expertise to study design, analysis, and evaluation.
Contribute to the development and evaluation of AI-enabled tools and assessments, including studies of how well they work in practice.
Participate in proposal development for federal, foundation, and philanthropic funding, and help build partnerships with universities and research organizations.
Mentor postdoctoral fellows, junior staff, and interns.
Share findings through peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, technical reports, and formats suited to practitioners and other non-technical audiences.

This position will be located in Princeton, NJ

Education

A Ph.D. or equivalent in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Data Science, Education, Psychology, Economics, or a closely related quantitative field with at least eight years of experience in an academic, industry, or applied research setting is required

Experience And Skills

Demonstrated expertise in artificial intelligence, machine learning, statistics, or a closely related quantitative area.
Strong record of research productivity, including peer-reviewed publications, conference papers, or technical reports.
Proficiency in Python or R, and experience working with large or complex data, such as model outputs, text, process and log data, or survey and administrative data.
Ability to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams and to communicate technical work clearly to non-technical audiences.
Commitment to the fair and responsible use of AI for all learners.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building or evaluating AI systems for education, such as tutors, feedback tools, scoring engines, or conversational agents.
Experience designing benchmarks or evaluation studies for AI systems, including the use of human ratings to validate automated judgments.
Experience with randomized trials, quasi-experimental designs, or other methods for causal inference.
Familiarity with educational measurement concepts such as validity, reliability, and fairness, or interest in learning them alongside the Center's psychometricians.

ETS is mission driven and action oriented

We are passionate about hiring innovative thinkers who believe in the promise of education and lifelong learning.
We are energized by cultivating growth, innovation, and continuous transformation for the next generation of rising professionals as leaders. Â In support of this ETS offers multiple Business Resource Groups (BRG) for you to learn and advance your career growth!
