Job Details:

General Notes

This full-time (40 hours/week), benefits-eligible, fixed-term Research Engineering/Scientist Associate position is housed in the Persad Aero-Climate Lab (www.ggpersad.com) within the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences in the Jackson School of Geosciences at The University of Texas at Austin. The Persad Aero-Climate Lab investigates how regional aerosol emissions and atmospheric processes interact with the climate system to shape regional hydroclimate and climate risk. This appointment has an expected end date of May 31, 2027, and is focused on bringing an active multi-model climate analysis through peer-reviewed publication while supporting ongoing group research.

Purpose

The purpose of this position is to advance research in the Persad Aero-Climate Lab by completing an ongoing quantitative analysis of near-term aerosol uncertainty impacts on potential evapotranspiration (PET) and vapor pressure deficit (VPD) relative to greenhouse gas forcing using Regional Aerosol Model Intercomparison Project (RAMIP) global Earth System Model data, leading the resulting manuscript through peer-reviewed publication, and supporting related group data analyses.

Responsibilities

Primary RAMIP Data Analysis: Complete ongoing quantitative analysis of global Earth System Model (ESM) output from the Regional Aerosol Model Intercomparison Project (RAMIP) to isolate and estimate the impacts of near-term aerosol uncertainty on potential evapotranspiration (PET) and vapor pressure deficit (VPD) relative to greenhouse gas (GHG) forcing.
Manuscript Drafting and Peer Review: Lead the preparation of a peer-reviewed scientific manuscript detailing the RAMIP PET and VPD analysis, generate publication-quality figures and documentation, submit the manuscript for publication, and conduct follow-up analyses and revisions to address peer-reviewer comments.
Research Group Data Support: Support related data processing, diagnostics, and climate model evaluation across the Persad Aero-Climate Lab utilizing RAMIP datasets and shared group workflows.
Follow-On Exploratory Analyses: Scope and execute preliminary follow-on analyses investigating related aero-climate and hydroclimatic metrics as time permits.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Earth Sciences, Atmospheric Science, Climate Science, Environmental Science, or a closely related quantitative field (or completion of degree requirements prior to the appointment start date).
Prior hands-on research experience analyzing multi-model climate output from the Regional Aerosol Model Intercomparison Project (RAMIP) and global Earth System Models (ESMs).
Demonstrated experience computing and analyzing hydroclimatic and atmospheric demand variables—specifically potential evapotranspiration (PET) and vapor pressure deficit (VPD)—to evaluate near-term aerosol forcing uncertainty relative to greenhouse gas forcing.
Proficiency in scientific programming and large-scale climate data analysis tools (e.g., Python, NetCDF, xarray) applied to CMIP/RAMIP-formatted model ensembles.
Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex climate model results into publication-grade figures and technical scientific writing.

Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior research experience working with Persad Aero-Climate Lab data analysis workflows on multi-model intercomparison projects (such as RAMIP or CMIP6).
Familiarity with regional aerosol radiative forcing mechanisms and hydroclimatic response pathways.

Job Title
: Senior Research Scientist — Quantum Memory

Location

Division:

About Us: 

QCi is an innovative, integrated photonics company that provides accessible and affordable quantum machines to the world today. Our devices operate at room temperature and low power, and are deployed today across high-performance computing, AI, cybersecurity, and remote sensing applications. We are extending that same integrated-photonics approach to quantum networking and quantum-secure communications, building chip-scale building blocks — sources, modulators, detectors, and now quantum memories — on a shared thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform.

Scope of the Job:

QCi is seeking a Senior Research Scientist to lead the development of a chip-integrated quantum memory based on erbium-doped thin-film lithium niobate (Er:TFLN). Erbium's optical transition falls directly in the telecom C-band, making it uniquely suited to interface with fiber networks and with QCi's existing TFLN photonic integrated circuits (PICs) including the lasers, electro-optic modulators, and single-photon detectors already in development on this platform.
You will build the simulation module and own the experiment setup on memory characterization through cryogenic characterization of storage and retrieval, to integration with QCi's photonic chips and quantum-networking systems. This is a hands-on research role for someone who wants to take a solid-state quantum memory from first coherence measurements to a deployable subsystem.

Duties / Responsibilities:

Develop and optimize the light–matter interface between Er3+ ion ensembles and TFLN photonic structures for high-efficiency, low-noise photon storage and retrieval.
Implement and benchmark on-chip quantum memory protocols (e.g., atomic frequency comb, spin-wave storage, EIT) and characterize storage efficiency, fidelity, and coherence times.
Assemble and run cryogenic experiments (closed-cycle cryocoolers / dilution refrigerators) to measure spectral, hyperfine, and coherence properties of Er ions in TFLN, including the effect of applied magnetic and electric bias fields.
Collaborate with QCi's photonic IC design and fabrication teams to co-design memory-compatible waveguides, ring resonators, and electro-optic tuning elements, and to align on process and packaging constraints.
Model and simulate device performance — absorption, storage efficiency, added noise — using tools such as Lumerical, COMSOL, or custom Python/MATLAB code, and reconcile simulation with measurement.
Integrate the quantum memory module with QCi's broader QKD and quantum-networking hardware (sources, modulators, single-photon detectors, timing electronics), supporting system-level test and validation from prototype to field-deployable hardware.
Document methodologies and results, contribute to peer-reviewed publications and patent filings, and mentor junior scientists and engineers on the project.
Represent QCi's quantum memory work with partners, funding agencies, and at technical conferences.
Ph.D. in Physics, Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, or a related field.
3+ years of hands-on experimental research in quantum optics, AMO physics, or solid-state quantum photonics beyond the Ph.D.
Direct experience with rare-earth-doped solid-state systems (e.g., erbium, neodymium, praseodymium, ytterbium) for optical or quantum storage, or an equally strong quantum-optics background with a clear path into this area.
Hands-on experience with cryogenic systems and low-temperature optical measurements.
Experience designing for, or characterizing devices on, photonic integrated circuit platforms — thin-film lithium niobate strongly preferred.
Strong grounding in nonlinear and quantum optics, single-photon detection, and low-noise optical measurement techniques.
Proficiency in Python or MATLAB for instrument control, data acquisition, and simulation.
A track record of peer-reviewed publications in quantum optics, quantum information, or related fields.

Required Qualifications

Education

Ph.D. in Physics, Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, or a related field.

Job Description

The eScience Institute has an outstanding opportunity for an AI Engineer to join their team.

About This Opportunity

As part of the university’s AI@UW Initiative, the eScience Institute has an outstanding opportunity for an AI Research Engineer with strengths in research applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI). As a member of the newly formed UW AI Corps within our broader eScience Institute team and the AI@UW initiative, the AI Research Engineer will participate in expanding campus-wide opportunities at the intersection of AI, data science, and disciplinary domains through collaborative research, consultation, support of curriculum development, development of AI training programs and community building initiatives. The eScience Institute works with researchers and students in all fields across the University of Washington to answer fundamental and transformative questions. As the hub of data-intensive discovery on campus, we lead a community of innovators in the techniques, technologies, and best practices of data science and AI.

Positions within the AI Corps in the eScience Institute provide guidance and expertise to the University of Washington community, including students, post-docs, staff and faculty on the best-practices for, and appropriate application of ML, generative AI, and data science methods. In addition, they are expected to support researchers in developing AI workflows and provide guidance on selecting the appropriate tools and computational infrastructure to complete research tasks. These interactions may be structured around a set of programmatic and thematic activities that are core to the eScience Institute mission as well as developing technical tutorials and other university wide offerings.

The AI Research Engineer contributes directly to projects with real-world impact, solving complex research problems across disciplines using cutting-edge AI techniques, and involves working with faculty, staff, and students from across the campus in a variety of formal and informal settings.

Key Responsibilities

AI Research & Technical Collaboration (40%)

Collaborate with researchers across UW to advance research and scholarship rooted in AI and data-intensive methods, proactively proposing and executing practical solutions to research challenges.
Build AI system workflows, pipelines, and infrastructure to support research teams.
Serve as the go-to expert on AI tools, methods, and responsible use, advising on approaches that are technically sound, ethically grounded, and aligned with institutional values.
Contribute to collaborative research outputs such as publications, reports, and open-source tools that advance the field and amplify the Institute's impact.

Teaching & Community Engagement (40%)

Develop and lead workshops, short courses, and training programs that foster AI literacy and support thoughtful integration of AI into research design and execution.
Support faculty and staff in the creation and use of AI in educational settings.
Create user-facing resources including guides, tutorials, and code notebooks enabling researchers and students to learn and apply AI methods independently.
Participate in core Institute programs such as the Data Science & AI Accelerator.
Collaborate with campus partners including academic departments, AI@UW (campus-wide AI initiative), UW-IT (UW Information Technology), and UW Libraries to advance shared goals around research innovation and responsible AI integration.
Evaluate the effectiveness of educational offerings and iterate based on participant feedback and learning outcomes.

Organizational Service (10%)

Participate actively in core team meetings, planning activities, and Institute-wide initiatives.
Provide weekly office hours open to the campus community
Serve on standing and ad hoc committees contributing to shared governance and institutional health.

Ongoing skill development (10%)

Dedicate time to independent study and hands-on experimentation with emerging AI tools, models, and research methods relevant to the Institute's work.

Required Qualifications

To be considered for this opportunity your application must demonstrate you meet both the minimum qualifications and additional qualifications listed below. Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in a Research or Engineering Field
Four years of professional or educational experience using advance computational techniques.
Applicants who do not meet these qualifications WILL NOT be forwarded to the Hiring Manager.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience with appropriate application of ML, generative AI, and data science methods in several research areas.
Previous experience with collaborative open source software development.

Describe a workshop, tutorial, or training you designed or led. How did you decide what to include, and how did you know whether people learned the material?

Why does a role centered on supporting others’ research and learning appeal to you compared with a role focused on your own research agenda?

added.title: Senior AI Solutions Engineer, Business Transformation
added.description:
The Senior AI Solutions Engineer brings a track record of building and operating AI services directly, and uses that hands-on foundation to lead AI transformation across Business, Commercial, Supply Chain Management, and Staff functions. The role is part enabler and part builder: it raises what non-technical colleagues can do on their own, and personally leads the projects that go beyond their reach.

Responsibilities

As business teams develop their own AI capability, this role guides each individual and department to the right level of AI application for the work in front of them—from everyday use of conversational AI tools, to customized assistants built on them, to no-code and low-code development, and combinations of these. For each opportunity, the engineer judges what a colleague can build themselves, what enablement or training would get them there, and what warrants a proper engineering project—then reviews the resulting solutions and determines when they are ready to operate. That judgment matters more here than volume of code.

For a subset of the portfolio, the engineer serves as project leader: defining the technical stack and architecture, and driving delivery hands-on across advanced builds such as LLM-based applications, RAG pipelines, agentic AI systems, and multi-agent workflows. The position needs to communicate in every direction with local functions, IT, and leadership. These projects span multiple functions and move at different speeds, so a track record across diverse companies, projects, and customers is preferred over deep specialization in a single domain.

Qualifications

Education : Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Experience : Minimum of 10 years in software engineering, AI service development, or technology consulting, including at least 3 years building generative AI and LLM-based services and at least 2 years leading projects as the accountable owner. Candidates are evaluated primarily on a hands-on track record of delivering services and carrying them through to production, and on breadth of exposure across organizations and customers, rather than on degrees or research output.
Required Skills :
Demonstrated ability to lead a portfolio of concurrent projects—intake, prioritization, scoping, scheduling, stakeholder alignment, risk escalation, and outcome reporting.
Practical command of the range of AI adoption paths available to non-developers—conversational AI tools, customized assistants, and no-code and low-code development—with the judgment to match each business need to the right approach.
Ability to review solutions built by non-engineers, assess production readiness, and raise them to an operable standard.
Ability to define the technical stack and architecture for a project and drive it through to delivery, working with others where needed.
Strong proficiency in Python, with the ability to design, implement, and debug independently. SQL proficiency sufficient for data querying and transformation.
Hands-on work with prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic AI systems, and multi-agent orchestration frameworks.
Experience deploying an AI service used regularly by real users to a cloud (AWS or Azure) or on-premises environment and operating it in production, not limited to PoC or prototype stages.
Ability to build quickly with AI coding tools and to validate and refactor the generated code into production-ready form, with full responsibility for understanding, validating, and maintaining every piece of delivered code.
Working command of core software engineering practices: version control, containerization, CI/CD, and automated testing.

Technical communication and enablement: Ability to explain the reasoning behind technical judgments in language non-engineers understand, to guide colleagues toward improving their own work, and to say no to an approach constructively while offering a viable alternative. Comfort communicating in every direction—with business functions, IT, and leadership.
Learning and collaboration: Ability to quickly learn complex, multi-domain business environments—Commercial, SCM, and Staff functions such as Legal, HR, and Finance—and to work alongside those teams to connect their needs to practical technical solutions. Comfort operating as the primary on-site technical presence for AI transformation work at this site.
Cross-border collaboration: Willingness to coordinate with Korea-based team members as projects require, including occasional meetings scheduled across time zones.
Other skills: Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving. A practical, resourceful working style and the agility to thrive in a fast-paced, startup-like environment.
English Proficiency : Professional-level English communication skills are required, including the ability to lead meetings and negotiate with business stakeholders.
Preferred:
Experience designing and running AI literacy or technical training programs for non-engineering audiences, and measuring their adoption outcomes.
Experience bringing solutions built by business users with AI or no-code tools into production.
Consulting, systems integration, or agency background with exposure to many organizations and customer environments.
Experience embedding observability (logging, metrics, alerting) into production services and using those signals to improve system architecture.
Experience building and deploying services under enterprise constraints such as firewalls, proxies, and corporate authentication systems; familiarity with SSO, EAI, and API Gateway, and with IT infrastructure fundamentals (APIs, authentication, networking, and security).
Snowflake access control and data governance design; pipeline scheduling, dependency, and failure-handling design (Snowflake Tasks, dbt, Airflow, and similar); familiarity with MLOps concepts.
Experience reviewing and managing deliverables from external vendors or outsourced partners.
Projects launched and operated across multiple business domains, described with technical stack, scope of ownership, and operational outcomes.
Mentoring junior engineers or leading technical workstreams.
Regulated industry experience — biopharma, healthcare, or similar.

Work Authorization:
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Compensation & Benefits

The anticipated salary range for this position is $135,000 to $160,000. Actual compensation may vary based on factors including experience, qualifications, skills, and business needs.

In addition to base salary, SK Life Science offers a competitive benefits package, including a 401(k) plan with company match and medical, dental, and vision coverage. Benefits are subject to eligibility requirements and may be modified at the Company's discretion.

Excellent architecture documentation, communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.

Experience building AI-powered copilots, virtual assistants, intelligent search, document intelligence, recommendation systems, or workflow automation solutions.
Experience with autonomous or semi-autonomous AI agents and multi-agent systems.
Experience with knowledge graphs and graph-based retrieval.

Job Description

As a Data Solutions Architect, you will lead the design of secure, reliable, and cost-conscious data and analytics solutions for clients. You will translate business goals and existing system constraints into target architectures, guide engineering teams through implementation while remaining hands-on in the development, and explain technical decisions and tradeoffs to client stakeholders. Your work will span data integration, storage, modeling, governance, and analytics across modern data platforms in Azure.

Key Responsibilities

Collaborate with clients and internal stakeholders to design and implement scalable data engineering solutions using the Microsoft Analytics ecosystem.
Lead discovery, select architecture patterns, document tradeoffs, guide implementations, and is accountable for the overall technical design.
Deliver current-state assessments, target architectures, integration patterns, data models, migration plans, estimates, and technical decision records.
Develop and maintain data pipelines, ensuring efficient extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) processes for structured and unstructured data.
Apply best practices in dimensional modeling to create robust and scalable data models for analytics and reporting.
Leverage tools such as Python, dbt, and SQL to develop advanced data transformation and integration processes.
Optimize data storage and retrieval mechanisms to support high-performance analytics workloads.
Define approaches for access, sensitive data, data quality, lineage, deployment, monitoring, recovery, and capacity or cost.
Define hybrid analytics requirements, including connectivity and security, in partnership with cloud and security specialists.
Monitor and troubleshoot data pipelines and workflows to ensure accuracy, reliability, and performance.
Collaborate with analytics and BI teams to ensure seamless integration of data assets into Power BI and other reporting platforms.
Stay informed about emerging trends and technologies in data engineering and cloud analytics to enhance solution delivery.

Required Qualifications

At least 10 years of experience in data engineering, with deep expertise in the Microsoft Data and Analytics stack.
Multiple years of experience leading discovery, evaluating design tradeoffs, presenting recommendations, and guiding a delivery team.
Strong proficiency in SQL, Python, and data modeling techniques.
Working knowledge of data extraction patterns and best practices.
Experience with ETL tools and frameworks, such as dbt.
Solid understanding of dimensional modeling and its application in analytics.
Strong problem-solving skills with a focus on delivering scalable and efficient solutions.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with experience in client-facing roles.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Azure Cloud infrastructure, including hybrid analytics workload configurations and networking.
Certifications in Azure Engineering and Administration (e.g., Fabric Data Engineer Associate, Azure Administrator Associate, Azure Solutions Architect Expert).
Experience with Azure DevOps or GitHub for code repositories and deployment.
Experience with data vault modeling and data mesh architecture concepts preferred.
Familiarity with advanced analytics tools and concepts, including machine learning workflows.
Experience using approved AI-assisted development tools responsibly preferred.
Knowledge of additional data visualization tools such as Tableau, Qlik, or AWS Quicksight.
Experience with Agile methodologies for project management.

The pay range for this position is $100,000 to $182,400. This range represents a good-faith and reasonable estimate of the compensation the firm expects to pay for this position at the time of posting. Actual compensation will depend on a variety of relevant factors, including an applicant’s skills, experience, qualifications, professional certifications, work arrangements, geographic location, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range, and compensation decisions depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. added.title: Specialist Solutions Architect, Data
added.description:
Who We Are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Specialist Solutions Architects (SSA) are domain experts aligned to specific Stripe solutions and customer buying centers. We have in-depth knowledge of specific solution offerings and a deep understanding of customer challenges. We align with specialist product sellers on deals, advise the broader pre-sales team on complex opportunities, support pipeline development and revenue attainment, serve as an advisor on go-to-market sales plays, and provide critical insights to our product and engineering teams.

What You'll Do

You will collaborate closely with sales and pre-sales teams to drive pipeline and revenue targets, while also educating the product and engineering teams on market trends and strongly influencing the product roadmap. You will develop deep relationships with senior customer business leaders and grow Stripe's solution offerings with new and existing customers. As a subject matter expert, you will scale the broader organization by creating reusable assets and coaching others on complex, high-value opportunities.

Responsibilities

Act as a subject matter expert on Stripe's Data products (data pipelines/export, revenue and reconciliation reporting, and analytics tooling) to accelerate opportunities
Demonstrate a deep understanding of how businesses warehouse and model payments and revenue data — data pipelines into Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, and Databricks; ETL/ELT patterns; and how that data feeds financial reporting, reconciliation, and BI
Conduct deep discovery of customers' existing data architecture, warehouse, and reporting stack to architect solutions that align Stripe's Data capabilities with their analytics and finance requirements
Advise customers on how to design for complexity: multi-entity and multi-currency reporting, custom data models, integration with existing BI tools (Looker, Tableau, Sigma, Metabase) and ERP/GL systems, and data freshness/latency requirements
Create and share best practices and reusable assets such as reference architectures to enhance the quality and efficiency of the broader sales and pre-sales organizations
Partner closely with the Data product sales team and actively drive opportunities for Stripe's largest customers, leading solution strategy and owning key customer relationships
Serve as a "Voice of the Customer" to drive product and feature request prioritization
Identify product, industry, implementation, and competitive trends, and provide actionable insights to product stakeholders and sales to influence Stripe's Data product roadmap
Act as an escalation point to drive complex technical issues to resolution with Stripe's engineering team
Represent the technical health of the business on quarterly sales forecast calls and highlight deal blockers with proposed solutions
Support marketing events including executive briefings, conferences, user groups, and trade shows

Who You Are

You're capable of engaging in both business-level and technical conversations at multiple levels of a customer organization, including finance, data, and engineering leadership. You enjoy working on products that require deep technical understanding combined with business context, and you're as comfortable in a warehouse schema as you are in a revenue conversation with a CFO. You're excited to become an expert and to share that knowledge broadly.

If you meet the minimum requirements below, we encourage you to apply — the preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

7+ years of experience in a technical sales, pre-sales, or solutions architecture role, with a focus on data platforms, analytics, or financial reporting
3+ years of hands-on experience with data warehousing and pipeline architecture (e.g., Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks) and ETL/ELT tooling
Strong understanding of how payments and revenue data maps to financial reporting and reconciliation workflows
Experience working with or implementing BI/analytics platforms (Looker, Tableau, Sigma, Metabase, or similar)
Strong knowledge of software engineering and API integration patterns, including how data pipelines are built and maintained
Exceptional communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, comfortable explaining complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
A proven ability to build strong collaborative working relationships with business partners
Ability to deal effectively with ambiguity and thrive in an unstructured, fast-moving environment

Preferred Qualifications

Experience integrating Stripe or other RESTful APIs into data pipelines or web applications
Familiarity with complex reporting scenarios: multi-entity consolidation, revenue recognition data models, or usage-based billing data
Experience with SQL at an advanced level and comfort working directly in a customer's data warehouse during discovery
Experience as a subject matter expert in financial services, fintech, or a data/analytics vertical
Pre-sales experience with Enterprise customers

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $239,900 - $359,900. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

updated.title: Senior Software Engineer, ML Infrastructure
updated.description:
Who we are

Gatik is in the business of autonomous freight, and that business is already on the road.
Every day, Gatik’s autonomous trucks move freight for Fortune 50 retailers, grocers and consumer brands across Texas, Arizona, Arkansas and Canada, connecting distribution centers and stores and keeping goods moving. At the heart of it all is the Gatik Driver™, our proprietary Level 4 autonomous driving system, powered by scalable, interpretable AI and engineered to deliver safe, reliable, high-frequency freight operations.

Gatik’s momentum is real. With more than $600 million in contracted revenue and $200 million raised in our August 2026 Series D round, Gatik has taken one of the toughest challenges in autonomous technology and turned it into a proven commercial business.

And the market is paying attention. In 2026, Gatik earned a place on Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers list, and the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies. The Gatik Driver™ won an Edison Award for Advancements in Autonomous Driving, and Inc. named our Co-founder and Chief Engineer, Apeksha Kumavat, to its Female Founders 500 list.

There's a lot more road ahead, and some of the brightest, most driven minds in autonomous technology are building the next chapter at Gatik. We're taking on hard engineering problems, pushing the limits of what's possible and building on a commercial foundation that's already proven itself in the real world with some of the biggest companies in the world, like PepsiCo and Loblaw. If you're ambitious, love solving problems that matter and want to see your work make a real difference, you'll find plenty to get excited about here.

About the Team

Scaling our machine learning models with data and fast infrastructure is central to how Gatik’s autonomy stack keeps improving. The Scalable ML team builds the data generation, curation, orchestration, and distributed training infrastructure that lets our ML developers work efficiently with large volumes of real-world fleet data and simulated driving scenarios. The team sits at the intersection of ML Platform, Jobs Platform, Cloud Platform, and High Performance Computing, and partners closely with Gatik’s autonomy, simulation, safety, and data teams.

About the Role

As a Senior or Staff engineer on Scalable ML, you’ll design and build the systems that turn raw driving data from Gatik’s fleet into high-quality training and evaluation sets, run training and evaluation reliably at scale, and give engineers the metrics and tools they need to make confident release decisions for driverless operations. At the Staff level, you’ll also set multi-quarter technical direction and act as a technical bridge across teams that don’t report to you.

What You’ll Do

Build scalable data pipelines.
Design and maintain reproducible pipelines that discover, label, and organize driving scenarios from Gatik’s fleet and simulation, with versioning, provenance, well-designed train/validation/holdout splits, and clear data contracts.
Curate high-quality datasets.
Build balanced training and evaluation sets that cover the scenarios our trucks encounter across routes, weather, and traffic conditions, and analyze coverage, composition, and label quality to shape dataset and model priorities.
Scale training and evaluation infrastructure.
Build distributed training, inference, and evaluation pipelines with robust data loading, checkpointing, and experiment tracking that run smoothly on multi-tenant GPU clusters.
Drive MLOps best practices.
Implement model artifact management, experiment tracking, and automated model testing and deployment at a standard other teams across Gatik adopt.
Own the metrics.
Define, implement, and validate model and release metrics (precision, recall, F1, ROC AUC, calibration, and task-specific metrics) with the statistical rigor that safety-critical release decisions demand, and characterize how behavior evolves across software releases and scenario types.
Run thoughtful experiments.
Set up baselines, ablations, and holdout comparisons; quantify uncertainty; and communicate results that help the autonomy team decide with confidence.
Build tools engineers love.
Develop dashboards and services for comparing software versions, exploring results at the scenario level, visualizing model outputs, and gathering reviewer feedback.
Shape shared infrastructure.
Partner with ML Platform, Jobs Platform, Cloud Platform, and HPC engineers to design and review changes to GPU scheduling and quota, job orchestration, storage, and compute cost.
Raise the engineering and reliability bar.
Design clean interfaces between data, modeling, and product layers; champion testing, type checking, code review, and fast CI; and lead root-causing and prevention of incidents, including those that cross team boundaries.
Lead technically (Staff).
Define and drive multi-quarter technical strategy for data and training infrastructure, represent Scalable ML in architecture discussions, and mentor engineers across the team.

What You’ll Need to Succeed

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field and 5+ years of relevant industry experience (or a Master’s degree and 3+ years). Staff candidates typically bring 8+ years, including time setting technical direction beyond a single team.
Strong Python software engineering skills, including designing modular, maintainable, high-performance, well-tested systems in a shared codebase.
Experience building end-to-end ML systems, from data pipelines and dataset curation through training, evaluation, and production, using tools such as SQL, pandas, PyTorch, or scikit-learn.
Hands-on production experience with Ray (Ray Core, Ray Data, Ray Train, and/or Ray Tune), including running and debugging Ray workloads at scale.
Deep experience with PyTorch and PyTorch Lightning for large-scale training, including distributed strategies such as DDP or FSDP, mixed precision, and checkpointing.
Experience designing and operating scalable ML infrastructure: distributed training and evaluation pipelines, experiment tracking, model serving, or large-scale distributed jobs.
Familiarity with shared-compute environments, such as GPU scheduling and quota, job orchestration, and multi-tenant clusters.
Solid grounding in statistics and experimental design, including choosing evaluation strategies, metrics, and thresholds that support real-world decisions.
Clear communication and the ability to work effectively across software, ML, and autonomy teams.

Salary Range:
$180,000 - $260,000

More about Gatik

Founded in 2017, Gatik has grown into a commercial force in autonomous freight, operating trucks daily in live customer networks across the United States and Canada. We're headquartered in Santa Clara, California, but our impact is felt on the roads and in the supply chains that keep essential goods moving for some of the biggest companies in North America.
Our trucks do some of the most demanding work in freight, running high-frequency, time-sensitive routes between distribution centers and stores, where reliability matters every single day. For our customers, that means more capacity, better service and products arriving where they need to be, when they need to be there.
Behind it all is AI-first technology built from the ground up for autonomous trucking, capable of navigating highways and surface streets and tackling the complexity of real-world logistics at scale.
Visit Gatik for more company information and Careers at Gatik for more open roles.

Notable News

For the latest company news, visit the Gatik newsroom.
Recent media coverage:
TechCrunch: Self-driving truck startup Gatik raises $200M following PepsiCo deal
Reuters: Gatik secures $200 million in funding as autonomous freight market accelerates

CNBC-TV18: No more test runs: Gatik says driverless trucks are now a real, money-making business
Forbes: Gatik And Loblaw Announce Largest Commercial Deployment Of AV Trucks

Taking Care of Our Team

At Gatik, we connect people of extraordinary talent and experience to an opportunity to create a more resilient supply chain and contribute to our environment’s sustainability. We are diverse in our backgrounds and perspectives yet united by a bold vision and shared commitment to our values. Our culture emphasizes the importance of collaboration, respect and agility.
We at Gatik strive to create a diverse and inclusive environment where everyone feels they have opportunities to succeed and grow because we know that together we can do great things. We are committed to an inclusive and diverse team. We do not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, national origin, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, marital status or any legally protected status.

Job Category

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

Join a team of 10 within Salesforce AI Labs, bringing computer-use AI into production with the autonomy of a small startup and the reach of Salesforce. We’re building Systems Integration Agent, announced at Dreamforce, which learns how to operate enterprise applications and turns complex workflows into reusable, code-backed automation. Customers are already running workflows in production; now we’re making that success repeatable across more systems and use cases.

Making computer use dependable raises hard engineering questions. How does an agent know it succeeded? When should it reason, and when should it follow a deterministic path? How should it recover when an application changes or ask for help before making a consequential mistake?

You’ll help answer those questions in production. Our team works directly with customers, building alongside them and turning discoveries into reusable product capabilities. As a Principal Engineer, you’ll remain hands-on while shaping architecture across our agent and backend systems, owning critical capabilities from design through operation, and helping other engineers deliver them.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Drive Agent Development & Architecture

Design and build systems that learn from demonstrations and combine AI reasoning with deterministic execution to complete workflows reliably.
Develop recovery and verification capabilities so agents can adapt to changes, confirm outcomes, and recognize when human intervention is needed.
Build backend services with robust workflow state management, failure handling, and secure access to customer environments.
Create evaluations and diagnostics that measure task success, expose regressions, and make failures understandable.

Build Directly With Customers

Work alongside customers to understand their workflows, prototype solutions, and validate results in their environments.
Investigate where automation succeeds or fails, then turn those findings into improvements to the core product.
Help customers move from their first successful workflow toward repeatable, increasingly self-service adoption.
Partner with forward-deployed engineers and product management to decide which customer needs should shape the roadmap.

Shape Technical Direction & Grow the Team

Lead architectural decisions across agent execution, backend services, and workflow state, aligning system boundaries and tradeoffs with other technical leads.
Evaluate model selection, tool use, and context management against reliability, latency, and cost.
Raise the engineering bar through hands-on implementation, design reviews, and mentoring; help engineers take on broader ownership and participate in hiring.

You're Our Person If...

You’ve led the architecture and delivery of complex backend systems through deployment, production failures, and subsequent improvements, with impact across multiple components or teams.
You have hands-on experience shipping and operating LLM-powered systems, and can explain how evaluations and production failures informed your design decisions.
You can reason through concurrency, persistent state, retries, and partial failures in systems that perform consequential actions.
You’re proficient in Python, Go, Java, or JavaScript/TypeScript.
You can turn an unclear customer problem into a bounded technical approach, test it with users, and lead it through production while creating capabilities other engineers can build on.
You want direct customer engagement to be part of your engineering work, including investigating problems and discussing technical tradeoffs.
You use AI development tools thoughtfully and take responsibility for the correctness, security, and maintainability of what you ship.

Even Better If…

Agent tool use, code generation, automated recovery, or evaluation frameworks.
Browser automation, workflow orchestration, or enterprise integrations.
Building an early-stage product or working in a customer-facing engineering role.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.
